prompt: What does `prompts/review.txt` ask the model to judge?

choices.text: The format and the category
choices.why: Right: urgency is not asked about, so it does not count here.

choices.text: The category and the urgency
choices.why: Urgency is not in the question.

choices.text: Whether the summary is a fair account of what the customer asked for
choices.why: The summary is not judged.

choices.text: Everything the triage prompt asked for
choices.why: It asks about two things, not all of them.

prompt: In `selfcheck.py`, which replies count as a flag? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A verdict that starts with WRONG
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: A verdict that starts with anything but OK
choices.why: Yes: `not said.upper().startswith("OK")`.

choices.text: A verdict of OK on a reply that is really wrong
choices.why: That is a miss, not a flag.

choices.text: A reply that `judge` finds wrong
choices.why: That is the person's side of the table.

prompt: Why does the lesson call a self-check *the same opinion asked for twice*?
hint: What does the reviewer know that the first call did not?

choices.text: The reviewer is shown the person's label
choices.why: Nobody shows it the label; it only sees the message and the answer.

choices.text: It reads with what it knew the first time, and nothing new
choices.why: Right: what it adds depends on what differs between the two readings.

choices.text: It runs at a higher temperature
choices.why: The review is not sampled.

choices.text: Because `selfcheck.py` calls the model twice per reply
choices.why: It makes one review call per reply; the phrase is about what the call knows.

prompt: On the temperature-0 run, the check flagged 45 replies and 18 of them were really wrong. What is its precision? Two decimal places.
Twenty-six replies were really wrong and the check flagged 18 of them. What is its recall? Two decimal places.
Flagging 45 of the seventy at random would give a precision of about 0.37. Why?

choices.text: Because a coin is right half the time
choices.why: Precision is not a coin's odds.

choices.text: Because the reviewer's precision was 0.37
choices.why: It was 0.40.

choices.text: Random flags hit wrong replies in the share they occur
choices.why: Right: 26 of 70.

choices.text: Because 0.37 is the share of replies that the reviewer flagged
choices.why: It flagged 45 of 70, 0.64.

prompt: The reviewer said `t07` was *not valid JSON because it is missing a closing bracket*. What did `pl show` reveal?

choices.text: A complete, valid reply
choices.why: Right: with the right category; the defect was invented.

choices.text: A reply cut off at the apostrophe of a word
choices.why: That is `t38`.

choices.text: A reply with an extra field nobody asked for
choices.why: It had the three fields.

choices.text: A reply in a code fence
choices.why: No fence.

prompt: Of the replies a check flags, the share that were really wrong is its ___.
Why is a flag that comes with a reason not more trustworthy for having one?
hint: Where does the reason come from?

choices.text: Reasons are cut off at 64 characters
choices.why: The printing is short; the problem is the content.

choices.text: The reviewer gives no reasons
choices.why: It gave one on every flag.

choices.text: A reason makes the verdict cost more tokens
choices.why: Cost is not the point.

choices.text: The reason is generated too, and here mostly invented
choices.why: Right: *missing a closing bracket* on valid JSON.

prompt: On the run with five samples per message at temperature 0.8, what recall did the same check reach?
hint: The last line of the table.

prompt: The slips argument says a reviewer should do better on a sampled run. Recall went only from 0.69 to 0.72. What does lesson 19 offer as part of the reason?
hint: How often did the samples agree?

choices.text: The sampled run had only forty messages
choices.why: Two hundred replies; recall is a share.

choices.text: The samples mostly agreed, so few mistakes were slips
choices.why: Right: little for the argument to work on.

choices.text: Sampled runs are always harder for a reviewer to check
choices.why: Not what was measured.

choices.text: The reviewer was sampled too
choices.why: It ran at 0.

prompt: On the sampled run, flagging 117 of 200 replies at random would give what precision?

choices.why: That is the coin's recall.
That is the reviewer's recall.
Right: the share of wrong replies.
That is the reviewer's.

prompt: What did *Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet* (Huang and others, 2023) find?

choices.text: Self-correction reliably fixed reasoning mistakes
choices.why: The title says the opposite.

choices.text: Little or no gain, and at times a right answer made wrong
choices.why: Right, and it noted that some earlier successes had relied on knowing from outside when an answer was wrong.

choices.text: Self-correction only works at temperature 0
choices.why: That is not what it measured.

choices.text: Models refuse to review their own answers
choices.why: They review them; the question is whether it helps.

prompt: You will ship at temperature 0. A colleague measured a self-check on sampled outputs. What do you conclude?

choices.text: Measure it again at temperature 0
choices.why: Right: a recall from one configuration says little about another.

choices.text: It will do better at 0
choices.why: Nothing says so.

choices.text: It will do the same at 0
choices.why: That is what needs measuring.

choices.text: Sampled measurements are always pessimistic
choices.why: There is no such rule.

prompt: `t38` is not JSON, and the reviewer said OK. What finds it every time?

choices.text: A second review at a higher temperature
choices.why: That adds noise, not a parser.

choices.text: A judge comparing it with another reply
choices.why: Nothing needs comparing.

choices.text: The person who labelled the case
choices.why: No person is needed for this.

choices.text: The `json` check, exactly and for free
choices.why: Right: `json.loads` fails.

prompt: Which of these can code check exactly, without a model? Choose all that apply.
hint: Anything with a right answer a program can compute.

choices.text: The reply parses as JSON
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: The category is one of the five labels
choices.why: Yes: membership in a list.

choices.text: The reply does not contain the canary word
choices.why: Yes: a string search.

choices.text: The category is the right reading of the message
choices.why: That is the one question a model check is for.

prompt: Your self-check has precision 0.40 and recall 0.69, and a coin would give 0.37 and 0.64. What should a flag do?
hint: What can it be trusted to do?

choices.text: Overwrite the answer with the one the reviewer would give
choices.why: It would act on 27 false alarms in seventy.

choices.text: Nothing yet: it is barely better than a coin
choices.why: Right: measure a better checker before it routes anything.

choices.text: Retry the triage call at a higher temperature
choices.why: The reviewer's flags do not say which replies to retry.

choices.text: Raise the answer's urgency
choices.why: The flag says nothing about urgency.

prompt: Which reviewer is most likely to catch the mistakes the answering model makes again and again?

choices.text: The same model, asked more politely
choices.why: Its view of the message has not changed.

choices.text: The same model at temperature 0.8
choices.why: Sampling the reviewer adds noise, not knowledge.

choices.text: The same model with the review prompt repeated three times
choices.why: Three identical readings are one reading.

choices.text: A different model, or one given new evidence
choices.why: Right: a reviewer with different blind spots misses different things.

prompt: Put the stages of checking a reply in the order this lesson recommends.
items: Code checks parsing, fields, labels and the canary
The model checks whether the label fits the message
A person reads what was flagged

prompt: Match each term to what it means in this lesson.

pairs.right: Share of flags that were really wrong
Share of mistakes that were flagged
A sample that missed the label the model favours
The model favours the wrong label

prompt: A team adds a self-check to a temperature-0 pipeline and reports that it *finds most mistakes*, from a demo of five sampled answers. What do you ask for first?
hint: What would this lesson's table look like on their configuration?

choices.text: Precision and recall against a person's labels, at temperature 0
choices.why: Right: measured on what ships, against labels nobody's model wrote.

choices.text: A longer review prompt
choices.why: Length is not evidence.

choices.text: Five more sampled answers
choices.why: More samples measure the wrong configuration better.

choices.text: The reviewer's own confidence in its verdicts
choices.why: Lesson 21 shows how far a stated confidence can be trusted.
